beats.lead: A trivia question that sounds made up.
beats.text: Is Oxford University older than the Aztec Empire?
beats.note: Not close. Oxford had scholars in residence for over three centuries before the Aztec Empire existed at all.

beats.name: University of Oxford
beats.role: The University's own recorded history: there is no clear founding date, but teaching existed at Oxford in some form by this year.

beats.lead: Meanwhile, the Mexica were still travelling.
beats.text: They didn't reach the Valley of Mexico and found Tenochtitlan, their future capital, until around 1325.
beats.note: That's already 229 years after Oxford had scholars in residence.

beats.lead: The Aztec Empire itself came later still.
beats.text: In 1428, after a succession crisis tore apart the region's dominant city, Tenochtitlan's ruler Itzcoatl forged a coup with two smaller cities.
beats.note: That alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan, known as the Triple Alliance, is what historians call the Aztec Empire.

beats.context: The gap between Oxford's earliest recorded teaching and the empire most people assume is the older of the two.

beats.line: Oxford was already old when the Aztec Empire was born.
